walkthroughs.body_html:
Graphic Communication — a core area of GCSE Design Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Graphic Communication brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Graphic Communication.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: In isometric projection, receding lines are drawn at what angle to the horizontal?
options: 30 degrees
45 degrees
60 degrees
90 degrees

mcqs.q: What does an orthographic drawing show?
options: Related 2D views such as front, side and plan
A single 3D pictorial view
Only the circuit diagram
The product rendered in colour

mcqs.q: Two-point perspective uses how many vanishing points?
options: Two
One
Three
None

mcqs.q: What is the purpose of rendering a sketch?
options: To show form and material using tone and texture
To add dimensions for manufacture
To calculate the cost of materials
To remove construction lines automatically

mcqs.q: What is the difference between isometric and perspective drawing?
options: Isometric drawing can only be done freehand without instruments.
Isometric keeps receding lines parallel at 30 degrees with no convergence; perspective makes receding lines converge to vanishing points so distant parts look smaller.
Isometric drawings have vanishing points just like perspective drawings.
The plan view is the project time plan attached to the drawing.

mcqs.q: In orthographic projection, what is the plan view?
options: The plan view is the front face of the product because it is planned first.
Isometric drawing can only be done freehand without instruments.
The view of the object seen from directly above, drawn in projection with the front and side views.
The plan view is the project time plan attached to the drawing.

mcqs.q: Does a 1:2 scale drawing show the object larger or smaller than real life?
options: Smaller — 1:2 means one unit on the drawing represents two units in reality, so the drawing is half size; 2:1 would be twice full size.
A 1:2 drawing is twice as big as the real object.
Isometric drawing can only be done freehand without instruments.
1:2 means two separate copies of the drawing are required.
